cohort: The study included 61,455 women with singleton gestations who delivered between 2007 and 2014 at a tertiary medical center, excluding pregnancies with fetuses diagnosed with chromosomal or structural anomalies.
finding: Maternal epilepsy is independently associated with adverse perinatal outcomes, including placental abruption, longer postpartum admission, neonatal intensive care unit admissions, neonatal seizures, transient tachypnea of the newborn, and respiratory distress syndrome.
